direction_note: Cycle 9 opened the external dimensions and both pre-registered tests died at stage A, each a clean and informative negative. (1) fx_surprise_against_crowd (calendar x CFTC positioning, EURUSD, 24 cells, three arms trading the surprise direction 15 minutes after a high-impact release): every against-crowd cell lost in design 2011-07 to 2017-12 (-0.005 to -0.143 R; -0.097 R, t -2.05 on 98 trades at q 0.8, z 1.0, same-day exit; -0.135 R, t -2.53 on 67 trades at q 0.9), every uncrowded cell lost (-0.056 to -0.173 R, t -1.75 to -2.81 on 77-224 trades) and the with-crowd cells were about zero (-0.046 to +0.080 R); the pre-registered asymmetry is reversed in sign (against minus with -0.05 to -0.15 R in six of eight cells); in check all arms sit near zero with mixed signs (-0.07 to +0.17 R, |t| below 1.5). A crowded leveraged-fund book is not forced out over the hours after an adverse surprise; the surprise-direction move from 15 minutes after the release to the close partially reverses in design and is noise in check. The fade mirror is snooped and not an edge (design gross about 0.06-0.10 R, gone in check); do not register it. (2) jpy_retail_dipbuy_fragility (TFX daily open interest, AUDJPY, 12 cells, short at the Tokyo open after a 5-day decline of 1 or 1.5 x ATR20 with heavy retail accumulation): every heavy cell lost in design, -0.24 to -0.44 R with t -2.1 to -2.7 (heavy10, k 1.0, 2-day hold: -0.264 R on 100 trades, t -2.70), while the light-accumulation control was about zero (+0.06 and +0.07 R at k 1.0; -0.02 and -0.16 at k 1.5), so heavy minus light was -0.19 to -0.40 R: the dips retail bought most eagerly were the ones that rebounded, the liquidity-provision reading of the 2011 BoJ Review, not a losscut cascade. In check the heavy cells were near zero with mixed signs (-0.18 to +0.09 R on 24-37 trades) and the light control turned negative (-0.20 to -0.28 R on 42-52 trades), so the heavy-minus-light difference flipped from -0.33 R to +0.38 R at the main cell: no stable relation between the retail-book state and the next days. The stable fact is that a short yen cross at the Tokyo open after a multi-day decline earns nothing or loses (10 of 12 cells negative over design plus check), the Tokyo-morning bounce seen intraday in cycle 3. Binding pre-registration R7: the long mirror (design t 2.1-2.7, check -0.09 to +0.18 R) is a snooped flip of the 2010-2017 carry-and-Abenomics regime and is never registered. Both judgments (scrap, with these lessons) are entered at the start of cycle 10. Programme status: 9 cycles, 222 registered hypotheses including two superseded by a session collision, no hypothesis has reached the pass bar, holdout untouched. Surprise x positioning and retail open interest are measured for these mechanisms. Remaining external avenues, each small: the implied-vol series as a daily state combined with positioning (the carry work used monthly VIX gates only), economic-momentum signals from the calendar actual values (needs a cross-sectional step the single-market engine lacks), and the weekly TFX long/short split as holdout-era conditioning for the parked basket. Recommendation to the user, now with nine cycles of evidence: the realistic route to an Alpha Swing pass is the sizing and risk design of the existing USDJPY basket, and the research loop should run only when a mechanism with a named, dated flow and a cheap instrument is on the table. The user stopped the 2-hour loop during this cycle; no cycle 10 is scheduled.

judgments.lesson: The reporting-season weekly excess on the Nasdaq 100 CFD is at most about +0.05 to +0.10 R per week over the same-year control and never reaches trade-level t 1 in design, so the index-side calendar risk premium is measured and closed. All 16 stage A cells on USATECHIDXUSD (design 2013-2017, check 2018-2023, Monday 14:30 to Friday 19:30 UTC hold): the best season cell by design t (start 17 days after the quarter start, 5 weeks, stop 2.0 x ATR20) made +0.062 R (t 0.83, 96 trades) against -0.039 R for its matching control, and the other three start_off 17 season cells +0.017 to +0.090 R (t 0.19 to 0.69), while all four start_off 10 season cells lost in design (-0.014 to -0.077 R), so whatever excess exists sits in the later reporting weeks and is a fraction of its own standard error. In check every season cell was positive (+0.055 to +0.192 R, t up to 1.44) against controls of +0.014 to +0.038 R, which is consistent with a small premium of the size the pre-registration expected (0 to +0.08 R) and which a weekly CFD hold costing 0.05 to 0.13 R cannot turn into a trade; the pre-registered rule 1 (trade-level design t >= 1 at the chosen season cell) failed as the honest prior said it would in two cases out of three if the effect is real at that size. With FOMC cycle, turn-of-month, option expiry, pre-holiday drift, overnight drift and now the earnings season measured, no index calendar premium passes on a retail CFD. Do not retry with other window offsets or week counts, a day-of-announcement-only hold (the Savor-Wilson macro-announcement-day premium is about 10 bp a day against a 3-5 bp CFD round trip, so even the clean version nets about +0.03 R and would need thousands of trades), the S&P 500 or Nikkei 225 as primary, or an options-implied version this data cannot trade.
judgments.notes: Killed at the automatic stage A floor (best design t 0.83 < 1) and at the pre-registered rule 1. The control design did its job: season minus control was +0.10 R in design at the chosen cell and about +0.04 to +0.15 R in check, a consistent sign with no power, exactly the inconclusive-negative outcome the rationale named as most likely. This was the last mechanism the Director could name from price, clock and calendar-date data; cycle 9 moves to the external series.

hypotheses.title: Positioning-amplified surprise continuation: trade in the direction of a high-impact scheduled data surprise 15 minutes after the release, only when CFTC leveraged funds are crowded on the other side of that surprise, holding to the New York afternoon of the release day or of the next weekday; with surprise-agrees-with-the-crowd and uncrowded control arms that trade the same surprises
hypotheses.rationale: Mechanism: a forced unwind, not an information drift. Who trades: leveraged funds (the CFTC Traders in Financial Futures 'leveraged funds' group: hedge funds and CTAs) holding a crowded directional book in a currency future, measured as the net position as a share of open interest ranked against its own last 52 weekly readings, known from the Friday 15:30 New York release. Why they must: a scheduled high-impact release that surprises against that book moves the price against them within the first minutes (Andersen, Bollerslev, Diebold and Vega 2003: the conditional mean reaction is complete in about five minutes, which is why this test does not trade the jump itself); risk limits, stop-losses, VaR and end-of-day marks then force position cuts, and large funds execute those cuts over hours (order splitting, waiting for liquidity), so forced flow keeps arriving after the first reaction. Evans and Lyons (2005, 2008) show that most of the exchange-rate response to macro news is transmitted through induced order flow spread over hours and days rather than through the instantaneous repricing, and Brunnermeier, Nagel and Pedersen (2008) show that crowded speculator positions in the CFTC data unwind abruptly and produce the negative skew of currency returns. Who is on the other side: dealers who warehouse the flow intraday and slower real money. Why it shows up in price only in that state: when positioning is neutral, or when the surprise agrees with the crowd, there is no forced seller or buyer after the first minutes, so the post-15-minute drift should be near zero; the hypothesis is the asymmetry between the arms, not the sign of post-release drift as such. What has been measured before: edge_hunt tested NFP follow and fade on USDJPY, EURUSD and gold (92 events, 1 to 3 hour holds, direction read from the first move, no surprise size and no positioning) and found nothing; cot_positioning tested eight standalone positioning rules (crowding fades, hedging pressure, one-week flow follow and reversal) and found nothing after weekly costs; cb_drift and fomc_cycle measured decision-day drift unconditionally; the news-inclusive arm of fx_liquidity_withdrawal_reversal measured fades of one-hour price moves on USDJPY with a two-hour exit, not surprise-signed trades. None conditioned a post-release trade on positioning, and the external README names positioning as a conditioning state. Costs: EURUSD median spread 0.35 pips, perhaps 0.6 to 1.0 pips in the quarter hour after a release; with 0.2 pips of slippage on each side and the 7 dollar commission (about 0.7 pips) the round trip is about 1.5 to 2.5 pips against a 1.0 x ATR20 stop of 50 to 105 pips (median 75), so about 0.02 to 0.03 R; the other five markets cost 0.03 to 0.05 R. Counts from the calendar and COT tables only (design 2010-2017, EURUSD, no price outcomes): qualifying releases with |dz| >= 1.0 split against / with / neutral as 101 / 113 / 235 at crowd_q 0.8 and 69 / 77 / 303 at 0.9; with |dz| >= 1.5: 49 / 51 / 127 and 32 / 33 / 162; GBPUSD 133 / 149 / 321, AUDUSD 137 / 132 / 260, USDJPY 76 / 81 / 240, USDCAD 136 / 126 / 318 at z 1.0 and q 0.8; about 414 release days a year-set on EURUSD, 1.25 qualifying releases per release day. Expected: the against arm +0.12 R (about 9 pips of drift on a 75-pip stop) with trade-level design t about 1.3 on about 100 trades at crowd_q 0.8 and z_min 1.0, the with arm and the neutral arm within +-0.05 R of zero after costs; P(design t >= 2 | effect real at +0.12 R) about 0.3, so a kill is weak evidence and a pass is strong evidence. Speed: about 1 trade a month per market in the against arm, about 5 a month pooled over the six markets but clustered on US release days, so the speed score at expectation is 0.12 x sqrt(5) = 0.27: this is an edge-recording test, it reaches the challenge speed bar only if the against arm earns +0.3 R or more, and even a below-bar positive result is useful as a timing filter on the parked USDJPY legs around releases. Human execution: wait for the release, read actual against consensus on the calendar, check the crowd state from the Friday COT report, place one market order 15 minutes after the release with a 1 x ATR20 stop, exit 20:30 UTC the same day or the next weekday; two to six orders a month across the pairs. Most likely failure: the unwind is finished inside the first 15 minutes (ABDV) or the dealers lean against it so the drift is below 0.05 R, or crowdedness measured weekly is too stale to identify the book that is hurt on the day.
hypotheses.rules:
All times UTC. M15 bars, stamped at the bar open and sparse; locate every time by timestamp (m.ts for opens, m.close_times() for closes), never by bar count. Loop over releases (a few hundred per market), vectorise everything else.

SYMBOL CONSTANTS: base = first three letters of m.sym, quote = last three. The COT currency is the non-USD one (EUR, GBP, AUD, NZD, JPY, CAD); cot_sign = +1 when it is the base (EURUSD, GBPUSD, AUDUSD, NZDUSD) and -1 when it is the quote (USDJPY, USDCAD). Raise for any other symbol.

CALENDAR EVENT SET: e = F.ext_series(m, 'calendar'); keep rows with impact == 'high', time_source == 'scraped' (rows with a typical or unknown release minute are useless for a 15-minute entry), finite surprise_z, currency in (base, quote), and an event name that does NOT contain (case-insensitive) any of: 'Crude Oil', 'Natural Gas', 'Inventories', 'Unemployment Claims', 'TIC Long', 'Votes', 'Asset Purchase Facility'. Use F.ext_subset(m, 'calendar', mask). Row direction for the pair: s_row = sign(surprise_z) x inv x side, where inv = -1 if the event name contains 'Unemployment Rate', 'Unemployment Change', 'Claimant Count', 'Net Borrowing' or 'Jobless' (a higher-than-forecast number is bad for that currency) and +1 otherwise; side = +1 if currency == base, -1 if currency == quote. Row weight w_row = |surprise_z|. Rows sharing one ts_avail (the same release minute) are merged into one release: dz = sum over those rows of s_row x w_row. A release qualifies when |dz| >= z_min; its trade direction dir = sign(dz) (+1 long the pair, -1 short). Process releases in ts_avail order.

POSITIONING STATE: c = F.ext_subset(m, 'cot', market == COT currency), rows in ts_avail order (ts_avail = 19:30 or 20:30 UTC on the Friday release). For row r with at least rank_weeks (52) rows up to and including r: rank_r = (number of those 52 rows whose spec_net_oi <= spec_net_oi_r) / 52, in (0, 1]; earlier rows have no rank. For a release at time T use the last COT row with ts_avail <= T; skip the release in every arm if that row has no rank. state = +1 if rank >= crowd_q, -1 if rank <= 1 - crowd_q, 0 otherwise. crowd_pair_dir = cot_sign x state: +1 means the leveraged funds are crowded long the pair, -1 crowded short, 0 not crowded.

ARMS (p['arm']): 'against': crowd_pair_dir != 0 and dir == -crowd_pair_dir (the surprise hits the crowded book); 'with': crowd_pair_dir != 0 and dir == crowd_pair_dir (the surprise agrees with the book); 'neutral': crowd_pair_dir == 0. Every arm trades in the surprise direction dir, so the first reaction, the costs and the event set are identical across arms and only the positioning state differs. Raise ValueError on any other arm value.

ENTRY: T = ts_avail of the release. sig = the first bar whose close time >= T + delay_min minutes (delay_min 15, so for a release on the quarter hour the bar that contains the release is the signal bar and the fill is 15 minutes after the release). Skip the release if sig >= m.n - 1, if close_times[sig] - T > max_delay_min (60) minutes (data gap), if the UTC date of bar sig differs from the UTC date of T, or if ATR20[sig] is not finite or <= 0. Market order at the next open: entry_long[sig] = True for dir +1, entry_short[sig] = True for dir -1; entry_type[sig] = 0; valid_bars[sig] = 1; the fill is at the open of bar sig + 1 (ask for longs, bid for shorts, plus slippage). One position at a time: the executor ignores an entry while a position is open, so a second qualifying release inside an open hold is not traded.

STOP: daily = F.daily_bars(m); ATR20 = daily.to_bars(F.atr_prev(daily, atr_n = 20)), the mean daily range of the previous 20 trading days, known at the day start; read at sig. sl_dist[sig] = sl_atr x ATR20[sig] (sl_atr 1.0, price units, > 0). tp_dist NaN (no target), max_bars 0.

EXIT: exit date E = the UTC date of T for hold 'd0'; for hold 'd1' the next weekday (Monday to Friday) after the UTC date of T (a Friday release exits on Monday). target = E at exit_utc (20:30, i.e. 16:30 New York in daylight time, 15:30 in winter, well before the Friday close). xi = F.first_bar_at_or_after(m, E, 20, 30); if xi < m.n and xi > sig + 1: exit_long[xi - 1] = exit_short[xi - 1] = True (the position closes at the open of the first bar at or after the target). Causal fallback: for each signalled release k, set exit_long and exit_short True on every bar j with m.ts[j] >= target_k and j <= sig_(k+1) (the signal bar of the next signalled release, or m.n - 1 for the last one), so a missing target bar closes the position at the first bar after the gap and never carries it into the next release's trade; a marker on sig_(k+1) acts at the open of the next fill bar, where the executor checks only the stop, so the new trade is untouched. Leftover guard: exit_long[sig_k] = exit_short[sig_k] = True. Markers with no open position are ignored by the executor. No other exits, no other filters.

PARAMETERS (every one read from p): arm (grid 'against', 'with', 'neutral'), crowd_q (grid 0.8, 0.9), z_min (grid 1.0, 1.5), hold (grid 'd0', 'd1'); fixed sl_atr 1.0, delay_min 15, max_delay_min 60, exit_utc '20:30', atr_n 20, rank_weeks 52. Module GRID = the full 24 cells so the checker exercises every value. Spec grids: stage A on EURUSD runs all 24 cells (the 'with' and 'neutral' cells are control arms and run only there); stages B, C, the walk-forward and any holdout run arm 'against' only (crowd_q x z_min x hold, 8 cells). The Director sets specs/auto/fx_surprise_against_crowd.json after the review step so that stage_a.grid holds the 24 cells and grid holds arm = against only.

EXPECTED COUNTS (EURUSD design 2010-2017, from the calendar and COT tables, a check for the Builder and the checker): against / with / neutral about 101 / 113 / 235 releases at crowd_q 0.8 and z_min 1.0 before data-gap and overlap skips (fewer trades than releases where a second release falls inside an open hold); 69 / 77 / 303 at crowd_q 0.9; 49 / 51 / 127 at z_min 1.5 and crowd_q 0.8. A count far from these means the event set, the sign mapping or the rank is wrong. The calendar covers 2010-01 to 2025-04, so the check period is complete and the holdout is partial (noted for any promotion).

REPORTING (from the trades; all 24 stage A rows read from the trials table, stage 'A'): per cell the number of trades, avg R, trade-level t, release-date-clustered t (R averaged per UTC release date, then t over dates), mean fill spread in pips and as a share of the stop, by-year avg R, for design and for check; for the chosen against cell: the matching with and neutral cells (same crowd_q, z_min, hold), avg R split by news side (base-currency releases against quote-currency releases) and by event group (employment: Non-Farm, Employment Change, Claimant Count, Unemployment Rate, ADP; inflation: CPI, PPI, earnings; activity: PMI, ISM, retail sales, GDP, production, confidence, housing, trade; rates: rate decisions), the avg R after dropping the best ceil(N/10) release dates, and the per-year against-minus-with and against-minus-neutral differences in design and check.

pre_registered.kill_if: (1) Hypothesis-cell floor on EURUSD, applied by the Director from all 24 stage A rows in the trials table (stage 'A') even if the pipeline reports a candidate, because the automatic floor ranks every cell and a control cell can clear it: among the 12 'against' cells with at least 40 design trades, the chosen cell is the one with the highest trade-level design t (the pipeline's own ranking); it must have design avg R > 0 and trade-level t >= 1; if the automatic floor is cleared only by a 'with' or 'neutral' cell, the B/C output is ignored and the hypothesis is scrapped under this rule. (2) Asymmetry, the test of the mechanism: at the chosen cell, design avg R(against) minus design avg R(the 'with' cell with the same crowd_q, z_min and hold) must be >= +0.08 R, and design avg R(against) minus design avg R(the matching 'neutral' cell) must be >= +0.05 R; both differences must be > 0 in check (the stage A backtests span design and check). If the with or neutral arms earn as much as the against arm, the positioning mechanism is dead and whatever drift exists is unconditional post-release continuation; that is recorded as the lesson. Because the neutral arm's direction (the surprise sign) was fixed here before any run, a neutral arm that itself reaches design t >= 2 with check avg R > 0 may be carried forward once as a new pre-registered under-reaction hypothesis (counted trials), but never promoted from this run. (3) Breadth: at the chosen cell, design avg R > 0 on both base-currency-news and quote-currency-news trades, and design avg R > 0 after dropping the best ceil(N/10) release dates; an edge carried by one event type or one year is an episode. (4) Regime: at least 4 of the 8 design years positive at the chosen cell (2010 is thin because surprise_z needs eight earlier surprises per event). (5) Replication: at the chosen cell read from the stage B trials table, the pooled design avg R over the other five markets (equal-weighted over trades) must be > 0, and the pooled-check hard gate (avg R > 0 with >= 30 trades) and the walk-forward gate stand; a EURUSD-only result with the pooled others negative is scrapped as noise. (6) Costs: the hard gate (positive at 1.5x costs) stands; the fill spread as a share of the stop is reported; if the chosen cell is positive gross but negative net the lesson is that the post-release unwind is smaller than a 2-pip round trip. (7) Pass bar: design t >= 2 at the chosen cell with (2) satisfied in design and check; a positive result below that is recorded as below the bar and is not promoted. Speed: at about 1 trade a month per market and +0.12 R the score is 0.27 (about 5 trades a month pooled, correlated on US release days), so this is recorded as an edge unless the against arm earns +0.3 R or more; honest expectation +0.12 R, design t about 1.3, P(t >= 2 | real) about 0.3; most likely failure: the unwind is complete inside the first 15 minutes or dealers absorb it, leaving a drift below 0.05 R.

hypotheses.why_different: Every prior news or positioning test used one input alone. edge_hunt's NFP tests (inside prior_nasdaq_lead_lag) traded the direction of the first 15-minute move on 92 NFP days with 1 to 3 hour holds and no surprise size or positioning; cot_positioning's eight variants used positioning as a standalone signal at weekly horizons (crowding fades, hedging pressure, one-week flow follow and reversal) and found no edge after weekly costs; cb_drift and fomc_cycle measured decision-day drift without a surprise measure; the news-inclusive arm of fx_liquidity_withdrawal_reversal faded one-hour price moves on USDJPY and read nothing from the calendar. This hypothesis conditions a scheduled information shock on the state of the leveraged-fund book: the direction comes from the standardised surprise, not from the price move, so it is not a follow-the-move relabel; the entry waits out the five-minute repricing that ABDV measured; and the family carries two control arms that trade the same surprises in the same direction with the same costs, so a generic post-release drift or a generic cost effect appears in all three arms and only the forced-unwind component separates them. The pre-registered prediction is the asymmetry (against minus with >= 0.08 R, against minus neutral >= 0.05 R in design, both positive in check), which neither the price-only tests nor the positioning-only tests could have measured, and the external README explicitly reserves positioning for this conditioning use.

hypotheses.title: Retail dip-buying fragility: short a yen cross at the Tokyo open after a five-day decline of at least 1 x ATR20 during which the TFX Click 365 retail open interest grew by 10 or 15 percent or more, against a light-accumulation control (open interest up at most 2 percent on the same decline), holding 2 or 4 weekdays
hypotheses.rationale: Mechanism: latent forced supply from an underwater leveraged retail book. Who trades: Japanese retail margin traders, of whom TFX Click 365 is the exchange-traded slice (350,000 to 600,000 open USDJPY contracts in the design years; the OTC margin book is about ten times larger and behaves the same way). They are structurally long the yen crosses for carry and contrarian: they add longs as the crosses fall. Descriptive, design years only: AUDJPY daily open-interest changes correlate -0.26 with daily returns, open interest rises about 3.5 percent on down days and falls 2.2 percent on up days; on five-day declines of at least 1 x ATR20 the five-day open-interest growth has quartiles +4, +9 and +18 percent, so the retail book grows into almost every decline and the question is how much. Why it matters: the positions are 10 to 25 times levered with broker-enforced losscuts, so a book that grew heavily into a decline is latent forced supply: if the decline extends, losscuts fire in a cascade and the move accelerates (the BIS Quarterly Review of December 2019 attributes the 3 January 2019 yen flash crash in large part to Japanese retail losscuts; the August 2015 and January-February 2016 yen-cross drops showed the same pattern), so after heavy accumulation into weakness the return distribution of the cross over the next days is negatively skewed and a short has a positive expectation; after a decline that retail did not buy (the light arm, including days the book shrank, where the losscuts have already happened), there is no latent supply and no continuation is expected, or a bounce. Who is on the other side: real money and CTAs selling the carry, whose selling retail absorbs. The 2011 Bank of Japan Review found that retail margin traders dampen volatility in calm times, which says the expected edge is small outside stress and is why this test pre-registers a one-sided direction (fade the retail accumulation), a monotonicity check (15 percent >= 10 percent >= light) and a modest expectation. What has been measured before: cross_zfade found two-sigma moves on crosses keep running at the daily horizon; fx_volume_climax_reversal found one-day shocks on majors continue and tick volume is not a capitulation signal; trend_follow found price-only trend flat before costs; jpy_cross_losscut_after_us_shock found no Tokyo-session continuation after a US equity shock and a Tokyo-morning bounce instead, and its mirror long was banned as a snooped flip. None of those had a positioning measure; this test conditions on the retail book itself, has no equity shock, holds for days rather than one session, and carries a control arm (the same decline without accumulation) that isolates the retail-book effect from the plain decline. Costs: AUDJPY spread 0.9 pips, 0.2 pips of slippage each side, 7 dollars commission (about 0.9 pips), about 2.2 pips against a 1.0 x ATR20 stop of 58 to 127 pips (median 81), so about 0.03 R; swap on a short AUDJPY is about -0.4 pips a day in the design years, negligible. Counts (design 2010-2017, from the TFX and price tables, no outcomes): AUDJPY about 460 days with a five-day decline of at least 1 x ATR20 (about 270 at 1.5 x); heavy10 covers about 45 percent of them, heavy15 about 30 percent, light (growth <= 2 percent) about 15 percent; with one position at a time and 2 to 4 weekday holds about 80 to 120 heavy trades and 30 to 45 light trades on AUDJPY; USDJPY, NZDJPY and GBPJPY similar; EURJPY's retail book was not structurally long in 2010-2017 (median five-day open-interest change on declines -2 percent), so it is the natural placebo market and is expected to show the weakest heavy-arm result. Expected: heavy arms +0.08 R, trade-level design t about 1.0 on about 100 trades, light arm at or below zero; P(design t >= 2 | effect real at +0.08 R) about 0.15, so an inconclusive negative is the most likely outcome, but this is the first measurement of the retail-flow dimension and its control fixes the baseline for every later TFX idea. Speed: about 1.1 trades a month per market, about 4 a month pooled over the four structurally long crosses (correlated), score 0.08 x 2 = 0.16: an edge-recording test that reaches the challenge speed bar only at +0.35 R. Human execution: one check of the TFX daily statistics after midnight UTC, one market order at the Tokyo open on the qualifying days, a 1 x ATR20 stop and a time exit two or four weekdays later at 20:30 UTC; a few orders a month. Most likely failure: the accumulation is the normal state of the book, so the heavy arms are the decline itself and the light arm is too small to tell; or the fragility shows only in the two or three crash episodes of the design years and dies in the breadth test.
hypotheses.rules:
All times UTC. H1 bars, stamped at the bar open and sparse; locate every time by timestamp (m.ts for opens, m.close_times() for closes). Loop over TFX rows (about 250 a year), vectorise everything else.

TFX ROWS: t = F.ext_series(m, 'tfx_daily'); keep rows with symbol == m.sym (the price-store symbol column; raise if none) in ts_avail order (ts_avail = Click 365 trading date + 1 day at 00:00 UTC). For row r (TFX date d_r): oi_g_r = oi_r / oi_(r-5) - 1 over the previous five TFX rows (oi_lookback 5); undefined when fewer than five earlier rows exist or any of the six oi values is <= 0.

PRICE CONDITION, from the store's own daily bars: daily = F.daily_bars(m) (trading days closing 17:00 New York); ATR20 = daily.to_bars(F.atr_prev(daily, atr_n = 20)), known at the day start. At the signal bar (below) the last completed trading day is D (the trading day before the one containing the signal bar). Require daily.date[D] == d_r (the Click 365 day d_r ends at the New York close of d_r, so the two venues describe the same day; skip the row when they do not match, which happens around holidays that one venue observes). drop_atr = (daily.c[D] - daily.c[D - ret_lookback]) / ATR20[sig] with ret_lookback 5 (five trading days). Condition: drop_atr <= -k (k 1.0 or 1.5). Skip if D - 5 < 0 or ATR20[sig] is not finite or <= 0.

BANDS (p['band']): 'heavy10': oi_g_r >= 0.10; 'heavy15': oi_g_r >= 0.15; 'light': oi_g_r <= 0.02 (the control: the same decline without retail accumulation, including days the book shrank). Raise ValueError on any other value. A row trades only if its band condition and the price condition both hold.

SIGNAL BAR AND ENTRY: T = ts_avail of the row (00:00 UTC). sig = the bar whose close time == T (the 23:00-00:00 UTC bar); if no bar closes exactly at T, use the first bar with close time >= T provided close - T <= max_delay_min (120) minutes and the bar's UTC date equals T's date, else skip (a Friday TFX row has T on Saturday and is always skipped). Short only: entry_short[sig] = True, entry_type[sig] = 0, valid_bars[sig] = 1; the fill is at the open of bar sig + 1 (normally the 00:00 UTC bar, 09:00 Tokyo) on the bid plus slippage. One position at a time: an entry while a position is open is ignored by the executor, so overlapping decline days produce one trade per hold.

STOP: sl_dist[sig] = sl_atr x ATR20[sig] (sl_atr 1.0, price units, > 0). tp_dist NaN (no target), max_bars 0.

EXIT: exit date E = the hold_days-th weekday (Monday to Friday) after the UTC date of bar sig + 1 (hold_days 2 or 4; weekends skipped, holidays not); target = E at exit_utc (20:30). xi = F.first_bar_at_or_after(m, E, 20, 30); if xi < m.n and xi > sig + 1: exit_short[xi - 1] = True (close at the open of the first bar at or after the target). Causal fallback: for each signalled row k set exit_short True on every bar j with m.ts[j] >= target_k and j <= sig_(k+1) (the signal bar of the next signalled row, or m.n - 1 for the last), so a missing target bar closes the position at the first bar after the gap and never carries it into the next trade; a marker on sig_(k+1) acts at the open of the next fill bar, where the executor checks only the stop. Leftover guard: exit_short[sig_k] = True. Markers with no open position are ignored. No other exits, no other filters.

PARAMETERS (every one read from p): band (grid 'heavy10', 'heavy15', 'light'), k (grid 1.0, 1.5), hold_days (grid 2, 4); fixed sl_atr 1.0, oi_lookback 5, ret_lookback 5, exit_utc '20:30', max_delay_min 120, atr_n 20. Module GRID = the full 12 cells so the checker exercises every value. Spec grids: stage A on AUDJPY runs all 12 cells (the 'light' cells are the control arm and run only there); stages B, C, the walk-forward and any holdout run band in ('heavy10', 'heavy15') only (8 cells). The Director sets specs/auto/jpy_retail_dipbuy_fragility.json after the review step so that stage_a.grid holds the 12 cells and grid holds the two heavy bands.

EXPECTED COUNTS (AUDJPY design 2010-2017, from the TFX and daily tables, a check for the Builder and the checker): about 460 qualifying decline days at k 1.0 (about 270 at 1.5) before the band split and the overlap skips; heavy10 about 45 percent of them, heavy15 about 30 percent, light about 15 percent; about 80 to 120 heavy trades and 30 to 45 light trades after the one-position-at-a-time rule. A count far from these means the symbol subset, the day alignment or the open-interest ratio is wrong.

REPORTING (from the trades; all 12 stage A rows read from the trials table, stage 'A'): per cell the number of trades, avg R, trade-level t, by-year avg R, mean fill spread in pips and as a share of the stop, for design and for check; for the chosen heavy cell: the matching light cell (same k and hold_days) and the other heavy band at the same k and hold_days, the avg R after dropping the best ceil(N/10) entry dates, the avg R of entries inside the three largest drawdown months of the design years against the rest, and the per-year heavy-minus-light difference in design and check.

pre_registered.kill_if: (1) Hypothesis-cell floor on AUDJPY, applied by the Director from all 12 stage A rows in the trials table (stage 'A') even if the pipeline reports a candidate: among the 8 heavy cells with at least 40 design trades, the chosen cell is the one with the highest trade-level design t (the pipeline's own ranking); it must have design avg R > 0 and t >= 1; if the automatic floor is cleared only by a 'light' cell, the B/C output is ignored and the hypothesis is scrapped under this rule. (2) Control difference and monotonicity, the test of the mechanism: at the chosen cell, design avg R(heavy) minus design avg R(the light cell with the same k and hold_days) must be >= +0.06 R and the same difference must be > 0 in check; and in design the heavy15 cell at the same k and hold_days must be >= the heavy10 cell minus 0.02 R (more accumulation, more fragility). If the light arm earns as much as the heavy arm, the decline and not the retail book carries the continuation, the lesson is that retail accumulation adds nothing to a plain multi-day decline, and no unconditional follow-the-decline hypothesis may be registered from this run (its sign would be read off the control arm). (3) Breadth: at the chosen cell at least 4 of the 8 design years positive, and design avg R > 0 after dropping the best ceil(N/10) entry dates; a result carried by the 2011, 2015 or 2016 crash months alone is an episode and is recorded as such. (4) Replication: at the chosen cell read from the stage B trials table, the pooled design avg R over NZDJPY, USDJPY and GBPJPY (equal-weighted over trades) must be > 0, and the pooled-check hard gate (avg R > 0 with >= 30 trades) and the walk-forward gate stand; EURJPY is the pre-registered placebo (its book was not structurally long in the design years) and is reported, not gated: a EURJPY heavy arm as strong as AUDJPY's is evidence that the signal is the decline, not the book. (5) Costs: the hard gate (positive at 1.5x costs) stands. (6) Pass bar: design t >= 2 at the chosen cell with (2) satisfied in design and check; a positive result below that is recorded as below the bar and is not promoted. Speed: at about 1.1 trades a month per market and +0.08 R the score is 0.16 (about 4 trades a month pooled over the four structurally long crosses), so this is recorded as an edge unless the heavy arm earns +0.35 R or more; honest expectation +0.08 R, design t about 1.0, P(t >= 2 | real) about 0.15; most likely failure: accumulation is the normal state of the book so the heavy arms measure the decline itself, or the fragility lives only in two or three crash episodes.

hypotheses.why_different: No prior test in the programme used a measure of the retail book; the TFX daily open interest was built on 2026-10-14 for this purpose and the external README names open interest rising on a down day as the retail-flow proxy. jpy_cross_losscut_after_us_shock was an intraday test (short at 08:00 JST after a US equity-session drop, exit the same Tokyo session) whose condition was an equity shock, whose horizon was hours, and whose lesson was that the crosses bounce in the Tokyo morning; this test has no equity condition, conditions on how much the retail book grew over a five-day decline, holds two or four weekdays, and predicts an asymmetry between heavy and light accumulation on the same decline, which the intraday test could not measure. cross_zfade, fx_volume_climax_reversal and trend_follow were price-only (z-score, one-day shock, Donchian) with no positioning state; their finding that daily moves tend to continue is the reason the control arm exists: the light arm carries the plain decline and whatever continuation it has, so only the retail-book component separates the arms. cot_positioning measured speculator futures positioning at weekly horizons; the retail book is a different population with the opposite behaviour (contrarian, carry-long) and a forced-liquidation mechanism of its own. The sign is fixed from the mechanism (fade the accumulation) and from the published flash-crash evidence, not from any prior run of this programme.

director.direction_note: Cycle 9 scraps the earnings-season premium with the lesson that index calendar premia on a retail CFD are measured and closed (season excess at most +0.05 to +0.10 R a week, design t 0.83 at best, check consistently positive but below the floor), and opens the external dimensions with two hypotheses. (1) fx_surprise_against_crowd: trade the direction of a high-impact scheduled surprise (merged standardised surprise |dz| >= 1.0 or 1.5) 15 minutes after the release, only when leveraged funds are crowded on the other side (52-week rank of spec net position / OI >= 0.8 or 0.9), hold to 20:30 UTC the same day or the next weekday, 1 x ATR20 stop; 'with' and 'neutral' control arms trade the same surprises; EURUSD primary (about 100 against-arm design trades), replication on GBPUSD, AUDUSD, NZDUSD, USDJPY, USDCAD; expected +0.12 R, t about 1.3, speed score 0.27 (edge-recording unless +0.3 R). (2) jpy_retail_dipbuy_fragility: short a yen cross at the Tokyo open after a five-day decline of at least 1 or 1.5 x ATR20 during which the TFX Click 365 open interest grew 10 or 15 percent or more, 2 or 4 weekday hold, 1 x ATR20 stop, with a light-accumulation (<= 2 percent) control on the same declines; AUDJPY primary, NZDJPY, USDJPY, GBPJPY replication, EURJPY placebo; expected +0.08 R, t about 1.0, speed score 0.16. Both have control arms, so after the review step the Director must edit specs/auto/<slug>.json so that stage_a.grid carries every arm (24 and 12 cells) and grid carries the hypothesis arm only (8 cells each), and must apply the pre-registered floor and asymmetry rules from all stage A rows in the trials table rather than from the pipeline's best cell. Honest status for the user: neither test is a challenge-speed candidate at its expected size; they are the first measurements of the surprise x positioning and retail-flow dimensions, and a below-bar positive on (1) would still be useful as a release-day timing filter on the parked USDJPY legs. If both are negative, the next cycles should test: the COT crowd state combined with the implied-vol series as a carry-crash timing condition (the carry work used VIX gates by month, never positioning x vol at the daily horizon); economic-momentum signals from the calendar's actual values (Dahlquist and Hasseltoft 2020), which needs a cross-sectional step the single-market engine does not have; and the weekly TFX long/short split as a holdout-era conditioning variable for the parked basket, which cannot be designed on 2010-2017 data. In parallel the user should be told plainly that after nine cycles and 220 trials no new edge has reached the pass bar, so the realistic route to a challenge pass remains the sizing and risk design of the existing USDJPY basket, which the programme should treat as a first-class track.

reasons: The idea deserves compute; the rules need fixing first. The mechanism is economic and new here: a scheduled surprise that hits a crowded leveraged-fund book forces risk-limit selling spread over hours. It is judged as an asymmetry between three arms that trade the same surprises in the same direction at the same cost. It is not a duplicate. edge_hunt traded the first-move direction on 92 NFP days with no surprise size or positioning (12 NFP cells, best t +0.53, which supports the near-zero neutral expectation). cot_positioning used positioning alone. cb_drift found no decision-day drift. The family is theory-set (24 cells, 8 in the hypothesis arm, within the 36 limit).

Rule bug, d0 exit before entry: the d0 target is 20:30 UTC on the release date, but NZD releases come at 21:45/22:45 UTC. On NZDUSD 77 of 668 qualifying releases (design+check, |dz| >= 1, with a COT rank) fill at or after 20:30 UTC. In design at q 0.8, z 1.0 that is 14 against, 10 with and 22 neutral releases. As written, the causal fallback marks every bar from the earlier target onward, so these become one-bar trades filled at the New York rollover spread.

Rule bug, overlap: the leftover guard exit[sig_k] closes the previous trade at the open of the next release's fill bar. But the executor registers an entry only when it is flat at the signal bar's close (executor.py, 'register this bar's signals' block), so the new release is not traded either. Overlapping holds are cut short with nothing in their place. This hits 10-30% of d1 releases (EURUSD q 0.8, z 1.0 design: against 15 of 101, with 21 of 113, neutral 45 of 172), and the arms then differ for a mechanical reason.

Counts and dates are off. The leveraged-fund (TFF) series in cot.parquet starts on 2010-07-20 (as-of), so the first 52-row rank is usable on 2011-07-15. Design trades therefore run 2011-07 to 2017-12, 6.5 years; 2010 has none. The EURUSD neutral counts in the brief (235 / 303 / 127) count releases with no rank as neutral. The rules skip those, which gives 172 / 240 / 94. The against and with counts match (101/113, 69/77, 49/51). The q 0.9, z 1.5 against cell has 32 releases and can never reach the 40-trade minimum.
Kill-rule typos: rule (1) speaks of 12 'against' cells, but the grid has 8 (crowd_q x z_min x hold). Rule (4), '4 of the 8 design years', has to count only years that have trades.

Power: on EURUSD alone each arm has about 85-160 trades. With an R standard deviation of about 0.8, the against-minus-with difference has a standard error of about 0.1 R, so the +0.08 R asymmetry gate barely tells real from noise. Pooled over the six markets (about 565-630 against trades after de-overlap) the standard error falls to about 0.05 R. The test of the mechanism has to be pooled before anything is promoted.

Trend confound: leveraged-fund crowding follows the trend (in cot_positioning only 16% of crowding fades went with 63-day momentum). So the against arm is mostly counter-trend and the with arm mostly with-trend. In strong-trend years such as EURUSD 2014-15, one day of trend drift is about 0.1 R on a 1 x ATR20 stop, which is the size of the effect being predicted. The asymmetry needs a trend diagnostic to be read.

Speed: the pooled against arm has about 8 trades a month (673 design releases in about 78 months at q 0.8 / z 1.0 over six markets). At +0.12 R that scores about 0.33, and less once you allow for the same US release hitting four or five pairs in the same minute. It needs about +0.25 to +0.3 R to reach 0.7. The second path, 'a timing filter on the parked USDJPY legs', is not pre-registered. This is an edge-recording test.

Costs are low: a 1 x ATR20 stop (EURUSD median 75 pips) against a round trip of about 2 pips is about 0.03 R. The exception is NZDUSD fills at 22:00 UTC from November to March, which sit on the New York rollover (2012-2017 median opening spread 3.8 pips, p90 8.4, against 1.3-1.4 pips at other hours). That adds about 0.04 R to those trades, and the pipeline's G4 gate needs every stage-C market positive at 1.5x costs.
reviews.revisions: BUILDER (implement exactly): (R1) Late releases: skip a release entirely (no entry, no markers) unless xi > sig + 1, where xi = the first bar at or after the exit target (E at exit_utc). For d0 this removes NZD releases at 21:45/22:45 UTC and any release whose fill is at or after 20:30 UTC. For d1 it never binds. (R2) Replace the leftover guard with a planned-hold de-overlap. Walk the qualifying releases of the active arm in ts_avail order. Keep a release only if it passes every skip rule and m.ts[sig] >= target_prev, the exit target of the last KEPT release; for the first kept release there is no condition. A dropped release sets no entry and no exit markers. A trade that was stopped early does not reopen the window. For kept releases only, set exit_long[xi_k - 1] = exit_short[xi_k - 1] = True, plus the causal fallback on every bar j with m.ts[j] >= target_k and j <= the sig of the next kept release (m.n - 1 for the last). Drop the separate leftover guard. With this rule the previous trade is closed at or before the open of the next signal bar, so the executor is flat when the next entry registers. (R3) PARAMS and GRID unchanged. DIRECTOR: (R4) After this review, edit specs/auto/fx_surprise_against_crowd.json as the hypothesis says: stage_a = {market: EURUSD, grid: all 24 cells} and grid = {arm: [against], crowd_q: [0.8, 0.9], z_min: [1.0, 1.5], hold: [d0, d1]}. apply_review writes the full 24-cell grid. Left that way, stage B picks each market's best cell from the control arms too, and G2, G2b and G4 would be computed on control cells. (R5) Restate the expectations: design trades start 2011-07-15. EURUSD design releases (against/with/neutral) are 101/113/172 at q 0.8, z 1.0; 69/77/240 at q 0.9, z 1.0; 49/51/94 at q 0.8, z 1.5; 32/33/129 at q 0.9, z 1.5. After R1-R2 the q 0.8, z 1.0 arms have about 98/106/162 trades (d0) and 86/92/127 (d1). (R6) Kill rule (1): 'among the 8 against cells'. Kill rule (4): at least 4 of the 7 years 2011-2017 positive (2011 = July-December only). (R7) Mechanism gate before any promotion: if the against arm passes B/C, run the matching with and neutral cells (same crowd_q, z_min, hold) on GBPUSD, AUDUSD, NZDUSD, USDJPY and USDCAD with end = 2024-01-01 (design and check only; counted as trials). Rule (2) is then judged on the pooled six-market trades: against minus with >= +0.08 R and against minus neutral >= +0.05 R in design, and both > 0 in check. The EURUSD stage A asymmetry alone is not enough. (R8) Breadth rule (3): give a merged release the news side of the currency with the larger sum of |surprise_z| among its rows. USDCAD has 136 merged USD+CAD releases (simultaneous 12:30/13:30 UTC data); report them also as 'mixed'. (R9) Reporting: each arm's avg R split by whether the trade agrees with the sign of the pair's 63-trading-day close-to-close change at the signal bar; NZDUSD NZD-news fills separately (fill spread in pips and as a share of the stop). (R10) Neutral-arm carry-forward: allowed only as a new hypothesis judged on the five markets where the neutral arm was never run, plus the holdout. Its EURUSD design and check results are spent and cannot count as its evidence. (R11) Strike the 'timing filter on the parked USDJPY legs' path; it is not pre-registered. Speed is judged by the monthly Sharpe of the pooled six-market R per month after costs, which accounts for the same-minute US-news correlation. Below 0.7 the result is recorded as an edge, not traded.
reviews.notes_for_builder: 1. Calendar rows: e = F.ext_series(m, 'calendar'). Build the mask with numpy over e.column('impact') == 'high', e.column('time_source') == 'scraped', np.isfinite(e.column('surprise_z')), e.column('currency') in (base, quote), and the case-insensitive exclusions on e.column('event') (None counts as ''). Select with F.ext_subset(m, 'calendar', mask). If no rows survive (the truncation leak test can cut the series), return the empty Signals. Contribution per row = surprise_z x inv x side (inv -1 for the listed unemployment and borrowing names). Group rows with an identical ts_avail; dz = the sum of their contributions. Never rescale dz, and never take a rank, quantile or z-score over the whole sample. 2. COT: c = F.ext_subset(m, 'cot', F.ext_series(m, 'cot').column('market') == ccy), in ts_avail order. rank_r = (count of v[r-rw+1..r] <= v[r]) / rw on spec_net_oi with rw = p['rank_weeks'], NaN for r < rw - 1. For a release at T: j = np.searchsorted(c.ts_avail, T, 'right') - 1; skip the release in every arm when j < 0 or rank_j is NaN. state +1 if rank >= crowd_q, -1 if rank <= 1 - crowd_q, else 0; crowd_pair_dir = cot_sign x state. 3. Raise ValueError on an unknown arm, an unknown hold or an unsupported symbol (cot_sign +1 for EURUSD, GBPUSD, AUDUSD, NZDUSD; -1 for USDJPY, USDCAD). 4. sig = np.searchsorted(m.close_times(), T + delay_min minutes, 'left'). Skip if sig >= m.n - 1, if close_times[sig] - T > max_delay_min, if m.ts[sig] is on another UTC date than T, or if ATR20[sig] is not finite or <= 0. ATR20 = daily.to_bars(F.atr_prev(daily, p['atr_n'])) with daily = F.daily_bars(m). 5. Exit target: E = the UTC date of T (d0) or the next Monday-to-Friday date after it (d1); target = E + exit_utc (F.parse_hhmm); xi = np.searchsorted(m.ts, target, 'left'). Keep the release only if xi < m.n and xi > sig + 1 (R1). 6. Planned-hold de-overlap (R2): a Python loop over the releases (a few hundred) is fine. Then set entry and markers for kept releases only: entry_long/entry_short[sig] by dir, entry_type 0, valid_bars 1, sl_dist = sl_atr x ATR20[sig], tp_dist NaN, max_bars 0. 7. Checker expectations, EURUSD design 2011-07 to 2017-12: about 98 (d0) / 86 (d1) trades for arm against, q 0.8, z 1.0; about 106/92 for with and 162/127 for neutral. Releases before 2011-07-15 have no rank and are skipped in every arm. 8. Read every tunable from p (arm, crowd_q, z_min, hold, sl_atr, delay_min, max_delay_min, exit_utc, atr_n, rank_weeks); no hard-coded 52, 15 or 20:30.

reasons: Worth one measurement. It is the first test of the tfx_daily dimension: a named forced-liquidation mechanism (a levered retail book that grew into a decline is latent losscut supply), a sign fixed before any run, and a same-decline control. It is not a duplicate. jpy_cross_losscut_after_us_shock conditioned on a US equity shock and held one Tokyo session; this conditions on the retail book itself and holds days. It does share that test's population, side and Tokyo-open short, and that test found the crosses bounce in the Tokyo morning after US-session selloffs (all 12 arms lost). That is a known headwind in the first hours of this trade.

Premise check on tfx_daily (descriptive, conditioning data only). The dip-buying signature, a negative yearly correlation between the daily return and the open-interest change, holds in every year 2010-2023 for AUDJPY (-0.40 to -0.78) and NZDJPY (-0.23 to -0.70). USDJPY's flips from 2017 (+0.36 in 2017, about 0 in 2018, +0.35 to +0.72 in 2019-2023, matching the weekly long_share of 0.19-0.37 since 2022). GBPJPY is about 0 in 2016-2017, and EURJPY is positive from 2013. As a result the USDJPY heavy bands never fire in 2018-2023 (0 qualifying days). Check evidence comes from AUDJPY (about 37 heavy10 trades at k 1.0, hold 2), NZDJPY (about 53) and GBPJPY (about 18). Even AUDJPY was only about half long on the first weekly reading (long_share 0.51 on 2022-11-22), so 'structurally long' is an assumption about the design years.

Rule bug: the leftover guard exit_short[sig_k] closes the open trade at the next qualifying row's fill bar. The executor registers that row's entry only if it is flat at the signal bar's close, so the new row is not traded either. Five-day declines qualify on runs of consecutive days, so most 2- and 4-day holds would be cut to about one day and every other qualifying day skipped. The hold the hypothesis is about would not be the one tested.

Counts are below the brief. Friday rows (20% of TFX rows) are skipped, and one-position holds de-overlap. On AUDJPY in design with the planned-hold de-overlap: heavy10 91/70 trades (hold 2/4), heavy15 61/45 and light 29/26 at k 1.0; 67/53, 49/37 and 21/18 at k 1.5. Trading Friday rows at the Monday 00:00 UTC open gives 100/76, 66/48 and 35/28 (k 1.0) and 73/57, 51/38 and 24/19 (k 1.5). At +0.08 R the expected design t is about 0.7-0.9, below the stage A floor of 1.0 more often than not even if the effect is real.

Control too small and confounded. With 19-35 light trades the heavy-minus-light difference has a standard error of about 0.2 R, against a +0.06 R gate. And retail buys bigger dips, so heavy days are deeper declines: on AUDJPY at k 1.0 the median drop is -1.89 ATR (heavy10) and -2.08 (heavy15) against -1.65 (light) in design, and -2.37 against -1.43 in check. A raw heavy-minus-light difference partly measures decline size. Pooled over the four crosses the light arm has about 240 design trades (standard error about 0.075 R).

EURJPY as a placebo inside spec.markets would enter the pipeline's automatic gates. Stage B picks its best heavy cell. If that cell is positive in design, its trades join the pooled check and walk-forward, and it must also pass the 1.5x-cost gate. A placebo must be able neither to pass the hypothesis nor to kill it.

The mechanism pays in the tail: the BIS losscut evidence is about cascades (2011-08, 2013-05/06, 2015-08, 2016-01/02, 2016-06). Kill rule (3) drops the best tenth of dates, so a real but tail-only effect fails by construction. That fits the speed goal, but the lesson has to be recorded as tail-only, not as no effect.

Speed is far below the bar: about 1 trade a month per cross, 0.16 at expectation, +0.35 R needed to reach 0.7. This is an edge-recording test, and its main value is fixing the baseline for the TFX dimension.

Costs are low: the AUDJPY opening spread at 00:00 UTC had a median of 1.2-1.4 pips (p90 1.8-1.9) in 2012-2017. The round trip is about 2.5 pips against a stop of about 81 pips, about 0.03 R. Swap on the short is small over 2-4 days.

A dropped row sets no entry and no markers, and a trade stopped early does not reopen the window. For kept rows only, set exit_short[xi_k - 1] = True, plus the causal fallback on every bar j with m.ts[j] >= target_k and j <= the sig of the next kept row (m.n - 1 for the last). T* = the first 00:00 UTC at or after ts_avail that falls on Monday to Friday: T* = ts_avail for Monday-Thursday rows and the following Monday 00:00 UTC for Friday rows. sig = the bar whose close time == T* (the 23:00-00:00 UTC bar; on Sunday night it belongs to Monday's trading day). Require the pooled four-cross heavy-minus-light difference to be >= +0.06 R in design and > 0 in check, computed within decline strata: -1.5 < drop_atr <= -1.0, -2.0 < drop_atr <= -1.5 and drop_atr <= -2.0, using the strata the cell's k admits and weighting by the heavy arm's trade shares. Report each arm's median drop_atr. The AUDJPY-only stage A difference is not enough. (R7) Breadth rule (3): list the removed dates. If they are the cascade months (2011-08, 2013-05/06, 2015-08, 2016-01/02, 2016-06) and the remainder is <= 0, record the lesson as 'retail-book fragility is tail-only at a 2-4 day horizon'. reviews.notes_for_builder: 1. Rows: tx = F.ext_series(m, 'tfx_daily'); mask = tx.column('symbol') == m.sym (the column can hold None; compare None-safe); rows = F.ext_subset(m, 'tfx_daily', mask).
